vision_features.image_context: A field view showing multiple soybean plants photographed from above at a slight angle. Visible plant organs include trifoliate leaves, stems, and developing pods. The plants are growing in sandy/bare soil with some crop residue on the ground. Multiple plants fill the frame.
vision_features.abnormalities:
1. Pods (upper-center and upper-right of image): Several pods appear to have turned dry, tan-to-pale-brown in color and look shriveled or flattened rather than plump and full. They range from approximately 20–40mm in length. Their texture appears papery and dry. No distinct border color; the discoloration is uniform across the pod surface. These pods are scattered across multiple branch nodes throughout the canopy rather than isolated to one plant. Some pods appear to have split or are partially open at the seams.
2. Small round pod (center-lower area): One small, still-green, rounded pod approximately 8–10mm diameter is visible, contrasting with the dry brown pods nearby — suggesting mixed developmental stages or arrested development in some pods.
3. Some leaves (left-center and lower-center): A few leaves show minor surface irregularities — slight puckering or uneven texture on the upper surface — but retain overall green color. These are scattered across several leaves, small in extent.
4. One leaf (lower-right): A small, roughly circular hole approximately 3–4mm in diameter is visible, consistent with a physical breach in the leaf tissue, with no surrounding discoloration.
vision_features.absences:
1. No visible powdery or dusty coating on leaf surfaces.
2. No yellowing or pale-green coloration visible on the leaves — foliage appears uniformly dark green.
3. No visible raised pustules, tiny dots, or thread-like structures on leaf surfaces or undersides.
4. No wilting or drooping of stems or petioles is apparent.
vision_features.summary: The plants display largely healthy, dark-green foliage but carry a notable number of dry, tan-to-brown, shriveled pods that appear papery and flattened across multiple plants in the canopy. The pods are the most severely affected organ, with their dried, deflated appearance being the single most striking visual feature. Mixed pod stages are present — a few small green pods are interspersed among the dry ones. Leaf tissue is mostly intact and green, with minor surface texture irregularities and one small hole on a single leaf.

For stem canker, initial symptoms are small, reddish-brown lesions near the nodes in the lower third of the canopy that expand into sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins; for pod and stem blight, the most characteristic sign is linear rows of black specks on mature soybean stems.. Knowledge-base entry for 'Phomopsis':
────────────────────────────────────────
Phomopsis-infected seeds are cracked and shriveled and often covered with chalky, white mold. Infected seedlings have reddish-brown, pinpoint lesions on the cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.. Small, angular, reddish-brown lesions surrounded by a yellow halo; as disease progresses, lesions often grow together to produce large, irregularly shaped dead areas.. Centers of older lesions frequently fall out, causing leaves to appear tattered; symptoms usually begin in the upper canopy on young leaves.. Early symptoms include seed rot and damping off; the most characteristic symptom is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, which can girdle the stem causing stunting or death..
